items.followUp: What is an explainable algorithm, and why is it useful?

rubric.why: Identifies that people can understand the algorithm or its decisions.
rubric.description: Defines an explainable algorithm as one whose logic or decisions humans can understand.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that its working or decisions are understandable to humans.

rubric.why: States that the algorithm can make clear why it produced a result.
rubric.description: Explains that it shows how or why a particular result was produced.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing the explanation of the algorithm’s result or decision.

modelAnswer: An explainable algorithm is an algorithm whose working and decisions can be understood by humans.
It helps show how or why the algorithm produced a particular result.

items.followUp: Define the Internet of Things and give one example of a connected device.

rubric.why: Identifies the IoT as a network of connected devices.
rubric.description: Defines IoT as a network of physical devices connected through the internet.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing internet-connected devices as a network.

rubric.why: States that the connected devices communicate or exchange data.
rubric.description: Explains that the devices collect and exchange data.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning communication, data collection, or data exchange.

modelAnswer: The Internet of Things (IoT) is a network of physical devices connected to the internet.
These devices can collect and exchange data with one another or with other systems.

items.followUp: What is cloud storage, and how can a user access it?

rubric.why: Identifies the internet as the means of accessing cloud resources.
rubric.description: Defines cloud services as computing resources provided over the internet.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking internet access with computing resources or services.

rubric.why: Gives examples of resources available as cloud services.
rubric.description: Mentions resources such as storage, software, or servers that users can access on demand.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for giving a suitable cloud resource or explaining on-demand access.

modelAnswer: Cloud services provide computing resources, such as storage, software, or servers, over the internet.
Users can access these resources on demand without having to own and maintain all the required infrastructure.

items.followUp: How does two-factor authentication make an account more secure?

rubric.why: Identifies that two verification factors are required.
rubric.description: Defines 2FA as a login process that requires two forms of verification.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that two verification factors are needed.

rubric.why: Provides a valid example of two different factors.
rubric.description: Gives an example such as a password plus a one-time code or biometric check.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a valid pair of different authentication factors.

modelAnswer: Two-factor authentication (2FA) is a security method that requires two forms of verification to access an account.
For example, a user may enter a password and then provide a one-time code sent to their phone.

items.followUp: What is one benefit of using email to promote a product?

rubric.why: Identifies email as the channel for sending marketing messages.
rubric.description: Defines email marketing as sending commercial or promotional messages by email.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying promotional or commercial email messages.

rubric.why: Identifies the audience and purpose of the messages.
rubric.description: Explains that businesses use it to advertise products or services to customers.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing its use to promote products or services to customers.

modelAnswer: E-mail marketing is the use of e-mail to send commercial or promotional messages to customers.
Businesses use it to advertise their products or services and communicate with customers.

items.followUp: Describe the main components of the Von Neumann architecture and their functions.

rubric.why: Identifies the stored-program concept, a key feature of this architecture.
rubric.description: States that instructions and data are stored in memory.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing the stored-program concept.

rubric.why: States the purpose of the memory unit.
rubric.description: Explains that memory stores data and instructions.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the memory unit’s storage function.

rubric.why: Identifies the main CPU units.
rubric.description: Names the Control Unit and ALU as parts of the CPU.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying both the Control Unit and ALU.

rubric.why: Identifies how data enters and leaves the computer.
rubric.description: Explains that input and output units communicate with the computer and its external environment.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning both input and output units.

modelAnswer: The Von Neumann architecture uses the stored-program concept: instructions and data are kept in the same memory.
The memory unit stores the data and instructions needed by the computer.
The CPU contains the Control Unit, which directs operations, and the ALU, which performs arithmetic and logical operations.
Input units enter data and instructions, while output units present the results.

items.followUp: Describe any four layers of the OSI model and state the function of each.

rubric.why: Correctly describes the Physical layer’s role in transmitting bits.
rubric.description: Physical layer: transmits raw bits through the physical communication medium.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming the layer and stating its transmission or medium function.

rubric.why: Identifies the Data Link layer’s handling of frames.
rubric.description: Data Link layer: organizes data into frames and supports communication between directly connected devices.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming the layer and describing framing or link communication.

rubric.why: Identifies the Network layer’s routing function.
rubric.description: Network layer: routes packets between networks and uses logical addressing.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming the layer and describing routing or logical addressing.

rubric.why: Identifies the Transport layer’s end-to-end communication role.
rubric.description: Transport layer: provides end-to-end delivery of data between devices.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming the layer and describing end-to-end delivery.

modelAnswer: Physical layer: transmits raw bits over the physical communication medium.
Data Link layer: organizes data into frames and manages communication between directly connected devices.
Network layer: routes packets between networks using logical addresses.
Transport layer: provides end-to-end delivery of data between devices.

items.followUp: Explain four ways digital technologies can help an entrepreneur start or grow a business.

rubric.why: Explains how digital tools help promote a business and reach customers.
rubric.description: Online marketing helps entrepreneurs promote products and reach potential customers.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing online promotion or customer reach.

rubric.why: Identifies online selling as a way to expand business access.
rubric.description: E-commerce allows a business to sell products or services online.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning online sales or e-commerce.

rubric.why: Recognizes that technology can make business operations more efficient.
rubric.description: Digital tools can automate tasks and improve the efficiency of business operations.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing automation or improved efficiency.

rubric.why: Explains how data supports business planning.
rubric.description: Data analysis can help entrepreneurs understand customers and make better business decisions.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking data or analysis to customer understanding or decision-making.

modelAnswer: Digital technologies allow entrepreneurs to market their products online and reach more customers.
E-commerce enables them to sell products and services through online platforms.
Digital tools can automate business tasks and improve operational efficiency.
Data analysis helps entrepreneurs understand customers and make informed business decisions.
